title: Announcement that the Salk polio vaccine was safe, effective and potent
summary: On 12 April 1955 Thomas Francis of the University of Michigan announced in Ann Arbor that Jonas Salk's polio vaccine was safe, effective and potent. The field trial involved nearly two million children. US polio cases then fell sharply, from an average of about 45,000 a year before the vaccine to 910 a year by 1962, and worldwide cases have since fallen by more than 99 percent.

uncertainty.note: Single-day announcement; the date is given in all three opened sources.

as_recorded.value: When the announcement came in Ann Arbor, Michigan on April 12, 1955,
Just three weeks previously, on April 12, Dr. Thomas Francis of the U-M's School of Public Health had made the momentous announcement.
